title: Longitudinal digital speech assessment in progressive supranuclear palsy
task: Develop machine learning models for digital speech biomarkers in progressive supranuclear palsy progression
key_results: Longitudinal speech features accurately predict concurrent and 3-month-ahead clinical severity scores; repeated measures correlation demonstrates sensitivity to disease trajectory over 12 months
comments: Well-designed prospective cohort study but modest sample size (n=32) and single disease variant (PSP-RS) limit generalizability.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Digital speech features track PSP-RS disease progression
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; longitudinal measures demonstrate sensitivity to changes in clinical severity

hypotheses.hypothesis: ML models can predict future clinical outcomes from speech features
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; models accurately forecast clinical trajectories at 3-month horizon

title: AI-driven multi-omics integration and virtual screening identify UFC1 as a druggable effector in chemotherapy-stressed colorectal cancer
task: Identify druggable targets in chemotherapy-resistant colorectal cancer via multi-omics integration
key_results: UFC1 amplification and elevated expression in chemotherapy-responsive CRC; lead compound AK968 shows ΔG = –25.07 kcal/mol binding affinity and synergistic enhancement of 5-fluorouracil efficacy
comments: Comprehensive pipeline from genomics to structure-based drug design, though clinical validation beyond in vitro CRC cell lines remains pending.

hypotheses.hypothesis: UFC1 expression correlates with chemotherapy sensitivity in CRC
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; elevated UFC1 in chemotherapy-responsive tumors with enrichment in malignant epithelial cells

hypotheses.hypothesis: AK968 inhibits UFC1 and enhances 5-FU efficacy
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; increased γ-H2AX foci and synergistic cell proliferation suppression in UFC1-dependent manner

title: Adaptive navigation control of a bionic robotic fish in complex Karman vortex street flow fields using an LSTM-DDPG hybrid strategy
task: Adaptive navigation control of bionic robotic fish in vortex streets via reinforcement learning
key_results: LSTM-DDPG achieves 88.3% task completion rate, 5.2 J/m energy consumption (45.3% lower than PID) at Re=500-1000; outperforms PID, DQN, and MPC in precision and disturbance rejection
comments: Physical prototype experiments validate simulation results, but limited to single fish; swarm coordination and real ocean deployment remain unexplored.

hypotheses.hypothesis: LSTM temporal prediction + DDPG adaptive control eliminates need for pre-built flow models
hypotheses.result: 88.3% task completion with 45.3% energy reduction vs. PID control across Re=500-1000

title: Secure electronic voting system based on blockchain with dilithium authentication and zero-knowledge proof verification
task: Post-quantum secure privacy-preserving blockchain-based electronic voting
key_results: 408 transactions/second throughput, 2.18 s average block finalization; framework integrates Dilithium signatures, zero-knowledge proofs, and nullifier-based double-voting prevention
comments: Evaluation limited to permissioned blockchain; scalability to millions of voters and voter coercion resistance not addressed.

model_io.model: Dilithium + Zero-Knowledge Proof + Smart Contract verification pipeline

hypotheses.hypothesis: Zero-knowledge proofs preserve voter privacy while smart contracts enforce rule compliance
hypotheses.result: Framework achieved practical balance between post-quantum security, privacy, and throughput

title: Heterogeneous traffic flow theory fundamental diagram model considering vehicle queuing characteristics and lane changing behavior
task: Heterogeneous traffic flow fundamental diagram modeling with CAV-HDV interactions
key_results: CAV platoon density shifts FD upward and delays congestion; extending max platoon length 4→10 vehicles increases capacity only marginally (4306→4507 veh/h); lane-change interval reduction critical for capacity maintenance
comments: Purely analytical-numerical framework without empirical validation on real traffic; assumptions on safety-distance rules and Markov chain vehicle following may not capture actual driver behavior.

model_io.model: MLMVISF-based Heterogeneous FD with Markov-derived following ratios

hypotheses.hypothesis: Increasing CAV platoon density reduces congestion through cooperative control
hypotheses.result: FD shifted upward with delayed congestion onset across tested penetration rates

title: RT-DETR-based object detection and parameter extraction for wireless signal spectrograms
task: Modulation recognition and parameter extraction from noisy spectrograms
key_results: RT-DETR outperforms YOLOv8/v10/v11 across SNR range -30 to 30 dB; achieves superior average precision, recall, and NRMSE for parameter extraction across nine modulation types
comments: Strong noise robustness claimed but comparison limited to YOLO variants; generalization beyond nine modulation types unclear.

model_io.model: RT-DETR with Transformer Intra-scale and CNN Cross-scale modules

hypotheses.hypothesis: Transformer-based feature interaction reduces local convolution limitations in multi-signal scenarios
hypotheses.result: RT-DETR reduced missed detections and false alarms versus YOLO variants

title: VLAN-aware hierarchical multi-agent protection framework for robust fault isolation and coordination in active distribution networks
task: Adaptive multi-agent protection coordination in DG-rich distribution networks
key_results: VLAN-aware hierarchical MAS improves protection selectivity and coordination reliability under bidirectional faults and dynamic reconfiguration on IEEE 39-bus test platform
comments: Validation limited to adapted single benchmark; scalability to larger grids and real-time performance metrics not provided.

model_io.model: Three-layer MAS (RA, CA, SA) with VLAN organization (SV, GV, DV)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hierarchical VLAN-driven design enables localized decision-making while preserving global coordination
hypotheses.result: Robust and selective fault clearance under structurally complex multi-source conditions

title: An energy efficient reliable machine learning based fuzzy fault tolerant model with self-healing routing in wireless sensor networks
task: Energy-efficient fault detection and self-healing routing in WSNs
key_results: CWSN-AI v4.2 achieves 99.2% intrusion detection rate, 12-18% PDR improvement, 22-31% network lifespan increase vs. LEACH/PEGASIS/TEEN/AODV/SEP; LightGBM binary classifier: 97.4% accuracy, 0.9982 AUC-ROC
comments: Evaluation against older protocols (LEACH, AODV); synthetic training dataset (200k samples) may not reflect real WSN failure modes; multi-episode Dyna-Q healing mechanism lacks detailed algorithmic description.

model_io.model: Hybrid LightGBM + Mamdani FIS fault classifier and Dyna-Q self-healing router

hypotheses.hypothesis: Hybrid LightGBM-FIS architecture simultaneously optimizes fault classification and cluster network organization
hypotheses.result: 97.4% classification accuracy with 22-31% network lifespan improvement

hypotheses.hypothesis: Trust-based IDS with attack-type-aware isolation improves packet delivery and network integrity
hypotheses.result: 99.2% detection rate across four attack types at trust threshold 0.50

title: Universal Planckian dissipation in the strange metal state of the cuprates
task: Explain universal Planckian relaxation rate in cuprate strange metals
key_results: Universal 1/τ requires optical plasma frequency squared scales linearly with hole doping p; reconciles universality with doping-dependent resistivity across entire doping range
comments: Elegant resolution of a long-standing puzzle via plasma frequency scaling, though the Anderson-Gutzwiller mechanism remains phenomenological.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Universal Planckian relaxation can be reconciled with doping-dependent resistivity

title: Phase reconstruction and causality in nano-FTIR signals based on the finite dipole model with Kramers–Kronig relations
task: Reconstruct nano-FTIR phase signals using Kramers-Kronig relations within finite dipole framework
key_results: FDM-KKR method yields analytical amplitude-phase relations agreeing with simulations; enables phase reconstruction from amplitude data; consistent with causality constraints
comments: Strong theoretical contribution bridging analytical modeling and near-field spectroscopy, though practical applicability to complex materials with multiple resonances requires further validation.

model_io.model: Finite Dipole Model (FDM) with Kramers-Kronig Relations

hypotheses.hypothesis: Phase can be reconstructed from amplitude via KKR within FDM framework
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; analytical approximations agree with simulated PMMA spectra
Confirmed; phase reconstruction consistent with Kramers-Kronig causality
